prompt: A photograph of a section of a wall painting in lime plaster, shot square on to the wall. The painting shows a boy leading a horse by a rope halter, both in profile, on a plain ground with a single tree behind them. The colour is soaked into the plaster rather than sitting on it, in a limited earth palette of ochre, red iron oxide, black and lime white. The plaster is divided into day sections whose joins run as faint seams across the picture. A network of fine cracks runs through the whole surface and in three places the plaster has fallen away entirely to bare rough render beneath. Salt bloom has whitened one lower corner. The surface is chalky and completely matte. Shot square on with a 50mm at f8 in soft raking daylight so the losses and the plaster relief read, natural colour.
medium_blurb: Pigment into wet lime plaster, cracked and lost.
